headline: AI won't finish your track for you.
body: Generative tools can spit out loops in seconds, but they can't make creative decisions about what your track is trying to say. The bottleneck was never speed — it's judgment.
pull: Tools generate options. Only you can generate meaning.

headline: You're referencing the wrong thing.
body: Most producers A/B against a finished, mastered record while still in the creative stage — comparing apples to a whole orchard. Reference for energy and arrangement first, loudness last.

headline: Perfectionism is procrastination in a nicer outfit.
body: Endlessly tweaking a hi-hat for an hour feels like progress. It isn't. It's often a way to avoid the harder, scarier decisions further down the arrangement.
pull: If you're polishing, ask what you're avoiding.

headline: Your unfinished folder isn't a failure log.
body: Every producer has a graveyard of 80%-done ideas. The issue isn't starting too much — it's never building a system that pulls ideas across the finish line.
pull: Unfinished tracks aren't wasted — they're untriggered.

headline: The 2-bar loop trap.
body: Looping the same 2 bars for hours feels productive but teaches your ear nothing about tension and release. Real arrangement skill comes from finishing full journeys, even rough ones.
pull: A loop tells you nothing about how a track breathes.

headline: Sound selection is a decision, not a search.
body: Scrolling through 400 kicks isn't sound design — it's decision avoidance disguised as diligence. The best producers narrow fast and commit, then shape what they've got.
pull: Narrow the search. Widen the shaping.
